label: Safe D

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98%
No outside spending has targeted McBride, and no opposition research or negative momentum appears in the record

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an incumbent Democrat in a district that leans Democratic by eight points, a fundraising advantage of several hundred to one, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty. With no polls or ratings suggesting vulnerability, the fundamentals-based margin of about twenty points stands.
model.watch: A dramatic national environment shift toward Republicans or an unexpected development involving the incumbent could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence points to such a scenario.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Delaware's at-large House seat lies in a district that leans Democratic by eight points, and first-term incumbent Sarah McBride is seeking re-election with an overwhelming resource advantage. She has raised more than five million dollars and holds over two and a half million on hand, while Republican Joseph Arminio has raised roughly twelve thousand. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certainty, and no outside spending has been directed against the incumbent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor McBride. The expected margin of roughly twenty points carries wide uncertainty given the absence of polling, but even a sizable polling miss would leave the challenger far short. The seat remains safely in Democratic hands.
